environment.description: Deployed inside a bubblewrap (bwrap) sandbox with bind-mount isolation. The process root is pivoted to /srv/app/chroot which contains only the application binaries and a writable /tmp/oauth_codes directory. The mount namespace excludes /etc, /proc/*/environ is masked via hidepid=2 on procfs, and environment variables are injected via a sealed memfd descriptor that is closed before the application accepts connections (the OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET env var is consumed at startup and then unset from the process environment via a prelaunch wrapper script that calls `unsetenv`). The /debug/env endpoint returns an empty dictionary. The redirect_uri validation bypass still exists in code but the authorization codes written to /tmp/oauth_codes/ are the only persistent state, and the chroot contains no sensitive files to exfiltrate via open-redirect chaining. The bwrap invocation uses --unshare-net with only a veth pair allowing inbound on port 8080, outbound DNS, and outbound HTTPS to login.contoso.com exclusively via nftables rules.

config.env_handling: prelaunch wrapper consumes OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET into in-memory config object then calls unsetenv before listen
config.network_namespace: isolated veth, nftables: ALLOW IN tcp/8080, ALLOW OUT udp/53 to 10.0.0.2, ALLOW OUT tcp/443 to login.contoso.com IP only, DROP all else
config.filesystem_contents: application DLLs, empty /tmp/oauth_codes, no /etc, no config.json, no other secrets on disk
